practice_claim: Before adopting any token-reduction transform on code shown to the agent (minification, comment/whitespace stripping, learned or continuous-latent compression), measure the end-task cost, and adopt only where the token budget genuinely binds. If repository context must be compressed, stay at mild ratios (~4x) and validate on generation and cross-file tasks, not just completion.

Build rules files up gradually from real need and keep them small; move everything else into path-scoped rules, on-demand skills, and subagents that load only when relevant, and operate below the model's 'dumb zone' through intentional compaction.

Before building any metric, manually review 100+ diverse raw traces with open-ended notes, annotate only the first upstream failure in each trace, cluster the notes into 5-10 themes, and aim the first mitigations at the phases/classes where the failure mass concentrates (planning and self-diagnosis in published base rates).

Impose a turn/iteration budget on agent loops: fixed at roughly the 75th percentile of the unrestricted baseline's turn distribution, or better, a small default budget with on-demand extensions, plus explicit exit conditions and backoff/fallback handling for flaky dependencies, rather than letting runs go unbounded.

Select detection methods by access level (training data: matching; logits: NLL/Min-K and order-canonicity tests; text only: prompting probes) and suspected channel (verbatim, paraphrase, cross-lingual); always run more than one, and never certify a closed model clean because detectors came back negative.

Detect implicit reward hacking by measuring reasoning effort: truncate the CoT at increasing lengths, force an answer at each cut, and flag runs where high reward is reached with a small fraction of the reasoning (large truncated-reward AUC).

Before acting on a benchmark ranking, re-run it under perturbation — semantically transformed problem variants (difficulty-shifted, recombined, rephrased) and harness perturbations (answer-choice reordering, alternative scoring methods) — and treat rank shifts under perturbation as the ranking's real uncertainty.

When using LLMs for error attribution at all, structure the trace into hierarchical context levels and aggregate multiple independent judge passes by consensus or confidence-aware weighting, feeding disagreement back to adapt the judge, instead of one all-at-once read or binary search over the trace.

Build a read-only replay harness over your own recorded arrival traces (arrival time, priority, claim, duration, outcome, review verdict) and replay identical traces under competing dispatch policies with arrivals held fixed; require any proposed optimizer to beat FCFS and a trivially-tuned priority sort on the same traces, keep a random-oversampling baseline in the protocol, and validate kernels on constructed instances with known optima.

Build retrieval chunks by recursively splitting large AST nodes and merging small sibling nodes under a size budget, so every chunk is a self-contained syntactic unit; do not use fixed-line-window chunking.

Run the same protocol on matched tasks the benchmark never used — a matched control set, a from-scratch private mirror matched on difficulty, or a retro-holdout twin validated by statistical indistinguishability gates — and report the public-private score gap as the inflation estimate.

Before publishing or acting on internal eval results, review the pipeline against the 44 catalogued questionable research practices (selective baseline choice, test-set peeking via repeated iteration, cherry-picked checkpoints, unreported prompt tuning) and the irreproducible-practice list.

Treat decoding configuration (greedy vs. sampling, temperature, best-of-N) as a first-class experimental variable: report it in the methods, and evaluate under both greedy and sampled generation before claiming a model comparison.

When quantifying contamination, choose the contamination metric by whether models actually benefit from the samples it marks contaminated (score delta on marked vs unmarked), instead of reporting raw overlap percentages.

Require the reviewer to commit a judgment before seeing the agent's answer, or delay/slow the reveal at high-stakes checkpoints; aim these scrutiny mechanisms at the fast accept-loop where the programmer already 'knows' the plan, not uniformly across exploration-mode use.
Model dependencies explicitly; let the scheduler fan out independent branches asynchronously; bound per-step time so one slow step cannot stall the batch.
Re-query the repository with each generation draft (or exploration result) instead of retrieving once up front; let intermediate outputs sharpen the retrieval query.

Inject lightweight static-analysis facts (call graph, inheritance, configuration dependencies) as plain-text annotations in the agent's view of the code, primarily to stabilize navigation across runs.

Before reporting, gating, or rewarding on a pass rate, strengthen the oracle: augment hand-written benchmark tests with generated inputs (LLM- and mutation-based, coverage-driven, or random tests sampled against a trusted reference patch), synthesize plausible-but-wrong patches and keep the tests that kill them, and manually screen a sample of 'solved' instances for solution leakage and tests too weak to verify correctness. Then re-adjudicate all results, including existing leaderboard submissions and any acceptance gate or reward signal, under the stronger oracle.

When creating private eval sets, forbid annotators from copying any web or LLM source, require citation of inspiration sources, verify each prompt is not web-searchable, and disqualify items that fail originality/difficulty/ambiguity review.
